newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices soar, trade brisk.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- Prices soar, trade brisk.

text.p: U.S. municipals climbed three-quarters to a full point in early afternoon, brisk trade on Thursday, as Treasuries rallied after the latest jobless data showed the best of all worlds--growth, but not inflation.
"We're just following the dog here," a municipal trader, referring to the vastly more liquid Treasury market.

While municipal bond trading tends to slow down in volatile markets, traders said deals were getting done despite the sharply higher prices and the fixed-income market's early close at 1500 EDT ahead of the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.
"There's been some going-away type of business and a lot of professional type trading," the trader added.
Discount bonds were in demand, which suggests market participants see room for prices to gain further, as they outperform in rising markets.
The buying interest was not clustered at the long end, but also included short- and intermediate-term paper.

Looking ahead to next week, new issuance was estimated at just over $2 billion, including almost $1.26 billion of negotiated sales and nearly $800 million of competitive sales, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

The biggest negotiated sale is a $150 million offering by the Sacramento Municipal Utility, followed by a $132 million sale by United Nations Development and a $110,000 million sale by North Carolina Municipal Power Agency.
The competitive list is led by a $265 million sale of general obligations by Washington on Wednesday, followed by a $70 million sale of general obligations by Memphis scheduled for the same day.

While the U.S. central bank reassured fixed-income markets by not tightening monetary policy when its policy makers met earlier this week, the market already had started to fret that the Federal Reserve might raise rates as soon as August. However, the latest report on job growth soothed those fears.

June nonfarm payrolls gained 217,000--just about 5,000 less than expected--while the unemployment rate edged up two-tenths of a percent to 5.0 percent. The U.S. Labor Department revised May's payrolls up to 166,000 from 138,000.

September Treasury bond futures leaped 1-2/32 to 113-4/32, while September municipal bond futures climbed 30/32 to 118-21/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures contracts at plus 177 ticks.

In the secondary market, where supplies shrank to about $1.4 billion, according to Standard and Poor's Corp, Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Airport Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5.4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.68 percent, NET, down six basis points.
And New Jersey Economic Development Authority Natural Gas Facilities Revenues of 2032, which pay 5.7 percent, were bid at 99-3/4, up 3/4 of a point.
